evidence.title: Postmortem: Helios load-test failure
evidence.text: # Postmortem: Helios load-test failure Hey team, just dropping the initial notes from our debugging session regarding the [[Helios]] environment issues we ran into yesterday. The Helios load-test failure was traced to a connection-pool exhaustion bug in the new Stripe usage-metering service under concurrent writes. When we ramped up the simulation to mimic peak traffic for Pulse, the metering service kept opening new connections without releasing them back to the pool properly during heavy transaction bursts. This directly starved the main database threads and cascaded into timeout errors across the rest of the stack. It's a pretty classic oversight, but definitely something we need to patch before we touch the [[Billing migration]] plans we discussed last week. I've opened a ticket to cap the pool size and implement aggressive backpressure on the client side. We'll rerun the suite once the fix lands in staging. Let's make sure we keep an eye on this in our next sync.

evidence.title: Aurora migration — risk assessment
evidence.text: # Aurora migration — risk assessment Hey everyone, dropping some notes here following our sync on the database infrastructure. As we push toward the [[Helios]] release next month, we need to make sure our underlying data layers can handle the spike in throughput without dropping events or spiking error rates on Pulse. Looking closely at the timeline and our current test runs, the main identified risk for the Aurora migration is replication lag under the increased session-write volume expected after the Helios launch. Since Pulse relies heavily on real-time session replay ingestion alongside continuous error tracking and performance analytics, even a brief delay in replica sync could cause temporary inconsistencies in the dashboard or back up our ingestion queues. We saw some minor latency spikes during the last load test when writes doubled, which points right to this bottleneck. Action items for this week: - Run another stress test simulating 3x normal write load against an [[Aurora migration]] staging cluster. - Check parameter tuning on the writer and reader instances to see if we can optimize the replication stream. - Coordinate with the frontend squad so we handle any potential read-after-write quirks gracefully in the UI if lag does creep in during peak hours. Let's keep discussions rolling in the main channel. I'll update this note once we have the new benchmark numbers back from staging.

evidence.title: Infra review — 2026-01-20
evidence.text: # Infra review — 2026-01-20 Good turnout today for the sync. Mostly went over the usual [[Pulse]] backend metrics, but we spent a good chunk of time diving into the current database setup and why everyone keeps getting paged at 3 AM. The main pain point continues to be manual maintenance on the self-hosted instances. Between disk space alerts, routine patching, and replication lag [[Helios]], the team is spending way too much time babysitting infrastructure instead of shipping features for [[Pulse]]. After looking at a few options, the team decided at the 2026-01-20 infra review to migrate the primary Postgres database from self-hosted to a managed provider (Aurora), to reduce on-call burden. Moving to Aurora should take a massive weight off the [[Aurora migration]] project backlog. We'll get automated backups, easier scaling, and—most importantly—fewer middle-of-the-night alerts for the engineering rotation. Will spin up a staging cluster next week to benchmark the read/write performance against our current setup. If the numbers look good, we'll draft a proper cutover timeline and share it with the rest of the crew.

evidence.title: Product roadmap — H1 2026
evidence.text: # Product roadmap — H1 2026 Here is our working outline for the upcoming half. The general focus for H1 2026 is on stabilizing our core data ingestion pipelines and improving overall dashboard responsiveness for larger teams. We want to make sure the core experience feels snappy before rolling out any major visual overhauls. A lot of this ties back to the ongoing work in [[Aurora migration]], which should give us the database performance headroom we need to support heavier query loads. On the feature side, we are currently tracking a few key initiatives. First, we need to finalize the scope for [[Helios]] so the design team can start exploring mockups by late Q1. Second, engineering has [[API v3]] on the docket as a background effort, primarily focused on cleaning up deprecated endpoints and improving developer documentation rather than rewriting the whole contract overnight. Customer feedback from the last few user interviews highlighted that session filtering still feels a bit clunky when dealing with high-volume noise. We should schedule a quick sync with support next week to pull some recent examples of those failing queries so the frontend squad has realistic test cases. As usual, this is a living document and will likely shift a bit once we lock in engineering capacity during our next planning retro. Feel free to drop comments or questions directly in the thread.

evidence.title: Weekly eng sync — 2026-02-05
evidence.text: # Weekly eng sync — 2026-02-05 Had our usual Thursday catch-up today. Everyone's mostly heads-down on their current iteration cycles. The frontend crew mentioned they're still poking around at some bundle size optimization stuff [[Aurora migration]]. Nothing major broke this week, which is always nice. Sarah's group [[Helios]] is continuing their work on cleaning up some legacy components in the event ingestion pipeline, mostly just chipping away at tech debt that’s been sitting there for a while. We talked briefly about the upcoming office snack restock—consensus is we need more sparkling water and fewer fruit snacks that nobody touches. After that, we spent a few minutes reviewing the general load balancer charts. Everything looked flat and green over the last seven days, so no fires to put out there. Quick reminder to everyone: remember to update your local dependencies before running the integration test suites, otherwise you'll hit weird caching issues. That was pretty much it. Short and sweet. Back to the code.
